title: Convection diagram sheet
subject: Science
unit: Spring 2: Reactivity (9F); energy transfer by heating
source: Seeded from science/y9 lesson 39 (Convection diagram sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 39: Convection and radiation. To understand how energy is transferred by convection in fluids and by infrared radiation

picture.alt: A thermal image of a house
picture.draw: Draw and label: Convection diagram sheet

questions.q: Explain why a radiator warms the whole room.
questions.a: Air by the radiator warms, expands, becomes less dense and rises; cooler air sinks to take its place, forming a convection current
questions.model: Air near the radiator heats up. It expands and gets less dense, so it rises. Cool air sinks to replace it. The loop carries energy round the room.

questions.a: Shiny surfaces reflect infrared back and emit little, keeping the person warm

questions.q: Can convection happen in a solid?
Draw a labelled diagram of the convection current in a room with a radiator, with arrows and the words 'less dense' and 'denser'.
questions.a: Arrows up from the radiator, across the ceiling, down the far wall, back along the floor; labels correct
questions.model: Teacher draws the radiator and the first rising arrow labelled 'warm air, less dense, rises'.

questions.q: Sunny window test: place a black and a white cup of the same water in the sun for 30 minutes with an adult. Predict and explain which warms more.
questions.a: The black cup: dark surfaces absorb infrared better.

questions.q: Explain sea breezes in the daytime.
questions.a: Land warms faster; air above rises; cooler air from the sea moves in to replace it.

questions.q: Big question: how does the Sun's energy cross space?
questions.a: By infrared radiation, which needs no particles.
